- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.10) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.  
- If model spikes sharply after a recent dip (e.g., +10%+ from prior low), true price often lags or reverses → cap forecast at 1–2 days above prior high.  
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > 0.00) → add 2–5% to forecast if recent 3-day avg > 70.0.  
- If model forecast mean is 2–3% below true outcome over 30-day horizon, apply upward bias correction by 1–2% per 5-day window.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative swings (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model tends to overreact → dampen forecast volatility by 15–20% in next 7 days.  
- Model often overpredicts 30-day mean when sentiment is weak → adjust forecast mean down by 1–3% if sentiment avg < -0.10 over last 7 days.
